sum: Start with an accumulator set to zero.
Visit each number once and add it to the accumulator.
reverse: Think about the order of characters at the ends of the string.
Walk backward through the string or reverse an array of its characters.
capitalize: Find the beginning of each word before changing case.
Split on spaces, transform each word's first character, then join with spaces.
longest: Keep the best word seen so far.
Replace it only when the new word is strictly longer, so ties keep the first word.
unique: Membership lookup is the repeated work here.
Use a Set while building an output array in the original order.
palindrome: Decide which characters should be ignored before comparing ends.
Normalize case and remove punctuation, then compare characters from both sides.
fizzbuzz: Check divisibility by both 3 and 5 before checking either one alone.
flatten: Each item is either a value or another array.
Recursively visit nested arrays and append non-array values to one output list.
chunk: Every group starts at a multiple of the requested size.
Advance through the input by size and slice each group, including the final short group.
countwords: A map can hold a running count for each word.
Treat empty text separately, then split on spaces and increment each key.
twosum: For each number, you know which partner would complete the target.
Store previously seen values with their indices and look up target minus the current value.
groupby: The output key is derived from each word.
Use the word length as a map key and append words to the matching array.
trap-water: Water above a bar depends on the tallest boundary on each side.
Move the pointer on the shorter side while tracking its highest bar so far.
edit-distance: Define the answer for prefixes of both words.
At each pair of prefixes, consider insert, delete, and replace; equal final letters need no edit.
longest-valid-parentheses: Remember the position before the current valid region.
Use a stack of indices; an unmatched closing parenthesis becomes a new boundary.
median-sorted-arrays: A merged array is easy but misses the requested complexity.
Binary search a partition in the smaller array and check the values beside both cuts.
minimum-window: A valid window needs character counts, not mere presence.
Expand until all required counts are met, then shrink from the left while it stays valid.
merge-k-arrays: Only the next value from each array can be the global minimum.
Put one candidate per array in a min-heap; after removing one, insert its successor.
word-ladder: Each one-letter change has the same cost.
Use breadth-first search and mark words visited when they enter the queue.
maximal-rectangle: Each row can extend or reset column heights.
Treat every row as a histogram and compute its largest rectangle with a monotonic stack.
contains-duplicate: You only need to know whether a value appeared before.
Add each value to a Set after checking if it is already present.
best-stock-trade: A sale can only use a price from an earlier day.
Track the minimum price seen so far and compare each later price against it.
product-except-index: The product on either side can be computed separately.
Fill output with prefix products, then multiply by a running suffix product.
subarray-target-count: A subarray sum is the difference of two prefix sums.
For each prefix, add the count of earlier prefixes equal to current minus target.
anagram-check: Equal length is necessary but not sufficient.
Increment counts for one word and decrement for the other; all counts must end at zero.
longest-distinct-span: A repeated character invalidates only part of the current window.
Remember its latest index and advance the left boundary past that occurrence.
merge-overlapping-intervals: Intervals are easiest to compare in start order.
Sort by start; extend the last merged interval when the next start is at most its end.
spiral-matrix: Keep top, bottom, left, and right boundaries.
Read each edge in order, then shrink that boundary; check crossings before each edge.
sorted-pair-sum: The input order tells you which direction changes the sum.
Start at both ends; increase the left index when too small, decrease right when too large.
widest-container: Area equals the shorter height times the distance.
Move the pointer at the shorter height, since moving the taller one cannot improve that width.
longest-one-run: Track how many zeros are inside a current window.
Expand right, then move left until at most k zeros remain; update the largest width.
staircase-count: The final move came from one or two steps below.
Store two previous route counts and sum them for each new step.
minimum-coins: An amount depends on one coin plus a smaller amount.
Initialize best[0] to zero; for each amount, try every usable coin and take the minimum.
nonadjacent-loot: At each position, choose between taking and skipping.
The take total uses the best answer two positions back; skip uses one position back.
balanced-brackets: The last unmatched opening bracket must close first.
Push openers onto a stack and compare each closer with the popped opener.
warmer-day-wait: Some earlier days are still waiting for an answer.
Keep indices of decreasing temperatures; pop them when a warmer day arrives.
sorted-insert-position: You need the first value that is not smaller than target.
Binary search a half-open range and move right boundary when nums[mid] is at least target.
rotated-array-search: At least one side of the midpoint remains sorted.
Detect the sorted half, then keep it only if target lies within its endpoints.
island-count: Each land cell belongs to exactly one connected component.
On unseen land, count one island and flood-fill its four neighbors while marking visited.
course-order-possible: A dependency cycle leaves every node in it blocked.
Count prerequisites, queue zero-count courses, and remove their outgoing edges; compare visited count to n.
